t.E242.agn: It breaks down soon after being added to a beverage; according to JECFA, the main breakdown products are methanol and carbon dioxide. In 1990 JECFA found its use acceptable for cold sterilisation in beverages at up to 250 mg per litre in accordance with good manufacturing practice. In its 2012 regulation, the European Commission stated that it was last evaluated by the Scientific Committee on Food (SCF) in 2001 and that its residues were considered harmless.
t.E242.body: It breaks down almost immediately in the drink into methanol and carbon dioxide, so it is mainly these breakdown products that reach the body. A person with normal eating habits metabolises 1,000–2,000 mg of methanol a day.
t.E242.eval: Used in beverages for cold sterilisation against yeasts and moulds; shortly after being added it breaks down mainly into methanol and carbon dioxide. In 1990 JECFA found its use in beverages at up to 250 mg per litre acceptable; in 2001 the EU Scientific Committee on Food (SCF) considered its residues harmless.
t.E242.found.1: Mixed alcoholic beverages containing less than 15% alcohol
t.E242.prod: It is a synthetic product (OIV International Oenological Codex).
t.E242.regx.0: Acceptable as a cold sterilisation agent in beverages at up to 250 mg/l.
t.E242.regx.1: Use extended to mixed alcoholic beverages containing less than 15% alcohol (14.2.8).
t.E242.summary: A preservative that breaks down shortly after being added to beverages. It is used to kill yeasts in fruit juices, iced teas and wines.
t.E242.what: It is a preservative that breaks down shortly after being added to beverages and provides cold sterilisation against yeasts and moulds.
